attractions.name: Sialkot Fort
attractions.description: The remains of an ancient fort with a history tied to the city's origins, offering a glimpse into Sialkot's past.

attractions.name: Iqbal Manzil
attractions.description: The birthplace and ancestral home of poet-philosopher Allama Muhammad Iqbal, now preserved as a heritage site.

attractions.name: Sialkot Sports Industry Tours
attractions.description: Sialkot is world-famous for manufacturing sports goods (footballs, gloves); some factories offer visitor tours.

attractions.name: Jinnah Islamia College grounds and old city bazaars
attractions.description: Historic bazaars in the old city known for leather goods, surgical instruments, and local crafts.

food_places.name: Sialkoti Kanji Wale (traditional drink stalls)
food_places.specialty: Kanji, a traditional fermented carrot drink popular in the region

food_places.name: Paratha and lassi stalls, old city

transportation.notes: Sialkot has its own international airport, mainly for expatriate/overseas travel

weather_info.climate_type: Semi-arid, continental climate with hot summers and cool winters

travel_tips.tip: Use the Sialkot-Gujranwala bypass road to avoid city-center congestion when passing through toward Lahore.
Sialkot International Airport offers a convenient alternative to Lahore for onward international travel, built through local community/overseas investment.
Sialkot is generally a calm, business-oriented city; standard precautions in busy market areas apply.
Visit the old city bazaars in the morning when shops are freshest and less crowded.

history.founded: One of the oldest cities in Punjab, with roots going back over 3,000 years
history.city_history: Sialkot has a long history as a center of craftsmanship, particularly in sports goods, surgical instruments, and leather products, trading globally for over a century. It is also famed as the birthplace of poet-philosopher Allama Iqbal, considered the spiritual father of Pakistan.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
